requirements.heading: DKIM-Quoted-Printable
requirements.text: The DKIM-Quoted-Printable encoding syntax resembles that described in Quoted-Printable [RFC2045], Section 6.7: any character MAY be encoded as an "=" followed by two hexadecimal digits from the alphabet "0123456789ABCDEF" (no lowercase characters permitted) representing the hexadecimal-encoded integer value of that character.

requirements.heading: DKIM-Quoted-Printable
requirements.text: All control characters (those with values < %x20), 8-bit characters (values > %x7F), and the characters DEL (%x7F), SPACE (%x20), and semicolon (";", %x3B) MUST be encoded.

requirements.heading: DKIM-Quoted-Printable
requirements.text: Note that all whitespace, including SPACE, CR, and LF characters, MUST be encoded.

requirements.heading: DKIM-Quoted-Printable
requirements.text: After encoding, FWS MAY be added at arbitrary locations in order to avoid excessively long lines; such whitespace is NOT part of the value, and MUST be removed before decoding.

requirements.heading: DKIM-Quoted-Printable
requirements.text: Use of characters not listed as "mail-safe" in [RFC2049] is NOT RECOMMENDED.

requirements.heading: Tag=Value Lists
requirements.text: Unencoded semicolon (";") characters MUST NOT occur in the tag value, since that separates tag-specs.

requirements.heading: Tag=Value Lists
requirements.text: Tags MUST be interpreted in a case-sensitive manner.

requirements.heading: Tag=Value Lists
requirements.text: Values MUST be processed as case sensitive unless the specific tag description of semantics specifies case insensitivity.

requirements.heading: Tag=Value Lists
requirements.text: Tags with duplicate names MUST NOT occur within a single tag-list; if a tag name does occur more than once, the entire tag-list is invalid.

requirements.heading: Tag=Value Lists
requirements.text: Whitespace within a value MUST be retained unless explicitly excluded by the specific tag description.

requirements.heading: Tag=Value Lists
requirements.text: Tag=value pairs that represent the default value MAY be included to aid legibility.

requirements.heading: Tag=Value Lists
requirements.text: Unrecognized tags MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: Signing and Verification Algorithms
requirements.text: Signers MUST implement and SHOULD sign using rsa-sha256.

requirements.heading: Signing and Verification Algorithms
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST implement both rsa-sha1 and rsa-sha256.

requirements.heading: The rsa-sha1 Signing Algorithm
requirements.text: The hash MUST NOT be truncated or converted into any form other than the native binary form before being signed.

requirements.heading: The rsa-sha1 Signing Algorithm
requirements.text: The signing algorithm SHOULD use a public exponent of 65537.

requirements.heading: Key Sizes
requirements.text: Since short RSA keys more easily succumb to off-line attacks, Signers MUST use RSA keys of at least 1024 bits for long-lived keys.

requirements.heading: Key Sizes
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST be able to validate signatures with keys ranging from 512 bits to 2048 bits, and they MAY be able to validate signatures with larger keys.

requirements.heading: Other Algorithms
requirements.text: Other algorithms MAY be defined in the future.

requirements.heading: Other Algorithms
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST ignore any signatures using algorithms that they do not implement.

requirements.heading: Canonicalization
requirements.text: A Signer MAY specify either algorithm for header or body when signing an email.

requirements.heading: Canonicalization
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST implement both canonicalization algorithms.

requirements.heading: Canonicalization
requirements.text: Further canonicalization algorithms MAY be defined in the future; Verifiers MUST ignore any signatures that use unrecognized canonicalization algorithms.

requirements.heading: Canonicalization
requirements.text: It MUST NOT change the transmitted data in any way.

requirements.heading: The "simple" Header Canonicalization Algorithm
requirements.text: Header fields MUST be presented to the signing or verification algorithm exactly as they are in the message being signed or verified.

requirements.heading: The "simple" Header Canonicalization Algorithm
requirements.text: In particular, header field names MUST NOT be case folded and whitespace MUST NOT be changed.

requirements.heading: The "relaxed" Header Canonicalization Algorithm
requirements.text: The "relaxed" header canonicalization algorithm MUST apply the following steps in order:

requirements.heading: The "relaxed" Header Canonicalization Algorithm
requirements.text: o Unfold all header field continuation lines as described in [RFC5322]; in particular, lines with terminators embedded in continued header field values (that is, CRLF sequences followed by WSP) MUST be interpreted without the CRLF.

requirements.heading: The "relaxed" Header Canonicalization Algorithm
requirements.text: Implementations MUST NOT remove the CRLF at the end of the header field value.

requirements.heading: The "relaxed" Header Canonicalization Algorithm
requirements.text: The colon separator MUST be retained.

requirements.heading: The "relaxed" Body Canonicalization Algorithm
requirements.text: The "relaxed" body canonicalization algorithm MUST apply the following steps (a) and (b) in order:

requirements.heading: The "relaxed" Body Canonicalization Algorithm
requirements.text: Implementations MUST NOT remove the CRLF at the end of the line.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The DKIM-Signature header field SHOULD be treated as though it were a trace header field as defined in Section 3.6 of [RFC5322] and hence SHOULD NOT be reordered and SHOULD be prepended to the message.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The DKIM-Signature header field being created or verified is always included in the signature calculation, after the rest of the header fields being signed; however, when calculating or verifying the signature, the value of the "b=" tag (signature value) of that DKIM- Signature header field MUST be treated as though it were an empty string.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Unknown tags in the DKIM-Signature header field MUST be included in the signature calculation but MUST be otherwise ignored by Verifiers.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: v= Version (plain-text; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: It MUST have the value "1" for implementations compliant with this version of DKIM.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: a= The algorithm used to generate the signature (plain-text; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST support "rsa-sha1" and "rsa-sha256"; Signers SHOULD sign using "rsa-sha256".

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: b= The signature data (base64; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Whitespace is ignored in this value and MUST be ignored when reassembling the original signature.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: bh= The hash of the canonicalized body part of the message as limited by the "l=" tag (base64; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: c= Message canonicalization (plain-text; OPTIONAL, default is "simple/simple").

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: d= The SDID claiming responsibility for an introduction of a message into the mail stream (plain-text; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The SDID MUST correspond to a valid DNS name under which the DKIM key record is published.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: When presented with a signature that does not meet these requirements, Verifiers MUST consider the signature invalid.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Internationalized domain names MUST be encoded as A-labels, as described in Section 2.3 of [RFC5890].

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: h= Signed header fields (plain-text, but see description; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The field MUST contain the complete list of header fields in the order presented to the signing algorithm.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The field MAY contain names of header fields that do not exist when signed; nonexistent header fields do not contribute to the signature computation (that is, they are treated as the null input, including the header field name, the separating colon, the header field value, and any CRLF terminator).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The field MAY contain multiple instances of a header field name, meaning multiple occurrences of the corresponding header field are included in the header hash.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The field MUST NOT include the DKIM-Signature header field that is being created or verified but may include others.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Folding whitespace (FWS) MAY be included on either side of the colon separator.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Header field names MUST be compared against actual header field names in a case-insensitive manner.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: This list MUST NOT be empty.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: i= The Agent or User Identifier (AUID) on behalf of which the SDID is taking responsibility (dkim-quoted-printable; OPTIONAL, default is an empty local-part followed by an "@" followed by the domain from the "d=" tag).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The syntax is a standard email address where the local-part MAY be omitted.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The domain part of the address MUST be the same as, or a subdomain of, the value of the "d=" tag.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Notably, the domain name need not be registered in the DNS -- so it might not resolve in a query -- and the local-part MAY be drawn from a namespace unrelated to any mailbox.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The Signer MAY choose to use the same namespace for its AUIDs as its users' email addresses or MAY choose other means of representing its users.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: However, the Signer SHOULD use the same AUID for each message intended to be evaluated as being within the same sphere of responsibility, if it wishes to offer receivers the option of using the AUID as a stable identifier that is finer grained than the SDID.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: l= Body length count (plain-text unsigned decimal integer; OPTIONAL, default is entire body).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: This value MUST NOT be larger than the actual number of octets in the canonicalized message body.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: q= A colon-separated list of query methods used to retrieve the public key (plain-text; OPTIONAL, default is "dns/txt").

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: If there are multiple query mechanisms listed, the choice of query mechanism MUST NOT change the interpretation of the signature.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Implementations MUST use the recognized query mechanisms in the order presented.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Unrecognized query mechanisms MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The only option defined for the "dns" query type is "txt", which MUST be included.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Verifiers and Signers MUST support "dns/txt".

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: s= The selector subdividing the namespace for the "d=" (domain) tag (plain-text; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Internationalized selector names MUST be encoded as A-labels, as described in Section 2.3 of [RFC5890].

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: t= Signature Timestamp (plain-text unsigned decimal integer; RECOMMENDED, default is an unknown creation time).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Implementations SHOULD be prepared to handle values up to at least 10^12 (until approximately AD 200,000; this fits into 40 bits).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: To avoid denial-of-service attacks, implementations MAY consider any value longer than 12 digits to be infinite.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Implementations MAY ignore signatures that have a timestamp in the future.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: x= Signature Expiration (plain-text unsigned decimal integer; RECOMMENDED, default is no expiration).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Signatures MAY be considered invalid if the verification time at the Verifier is past the expiration date.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The value of the "x=" tag MUST be greater than the value of the "t=" tag if both are present.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Receivers MAY add a 'fudge factor' to allow for such possible drift.

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: z= Copied header fields (dkim-quoted-printable, but see description; OPTIONAL, default is null).

requirements.heading: The DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: After encoding, FWS MAY be added at arbitrary locations in order to avoid excessively long lines; such whitespace is NOT part of the value of the header field and MUST be removed before decoding.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: The following definition MUST be used for any DKIM key represented in an otherwise unstructured textual form.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Other tags MAY be present and MUST be ignored by any implementation that does not understand them.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: v= Version of the DKIM key record (plain-text; RECOMMENDED, default is "DKIM1").

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: If specified, this tag MUST be set to "DKIM1" (without the quotes).

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: This tag MUST be the first tag in the record.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Records beginning with a "v=" tag with any other value MUST be discarded.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: h= Acceptable hash algorithms (plain-text; OPTIONAL, defaults to allowing all algorithms).

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Unrecognized algorithms MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: k= Key type (plain-text; OPTIONAL, default is "rsa").

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Signers and Verifiers MUST support the "rsa" key type.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: (Note: the "p=" tag further encodes the value using the base64 algorithm.) Unrecognized key types MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: n= Notes that might be of interest to a human (qp-section; OPTIONAL, default is empty).

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: p= Public-key data (base64; REQUIRED).

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Verifiers SHOULD return an error code for any DKIM-Signature header field with a selector referencing a revoked key.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: s= Service Type (plain-text; OPTIONAL; default is "*").

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Verifiers for a given service type MUST ignore this record if the appropriate type is not listed.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Unrecognized service types MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: t= Flags, represented as a colon-separated list of names (plain- text; OPTIONAL, default is no flags set).

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Unrecognized flags MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST NOT treat messages from Signers in testing mode differently from unsigned email, even should the signature fail to verify.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Verifiers MAY wish to track testing mode results to assist the Signer.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: s Any DKIM-Signature header fields using the "i=" tag MUST have the same domain value on the right-hand side of the "@" in the "i=" tag and the value of the "d=" tag.

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: That is, the "i=" domain MUST NOT be a subdomain of "d=".

requirements.heading: Textual Representation
requirements.text: Use of this flag is RECOMMENDED unless subdomaining is required.

requirements.heading: DNS Binding
requirements.text: All implementations MUST support this binding.

requirements.heading: Resource Record Types for Key Storage
requirements.text: Strings in a TXT RR MUST be concatenated together before use with no intervening whitespace.

requirements.heading: Resource Record Types for Key Storage
requirements.text: TXT RRs MUST be unique for a particular selector name; that is, if there are multiple records in an RRset, the results are undefined.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: The Signer/Verifier MUST compute two hashes: one over the body of the message and one over the selected header fields of the message.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: Signers MUST compute them in the order shown.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: Verifiers MAY compute them in any order convenient to the Verifier, provided that the result is semantically identical to the semantics that would be the case had they been computed in this order.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: In hash step 1, the Signer/Verifier MUST hash the message body, canonicalized using the body canonicalization algorithm specified in the "c=" tag and then truncated to the length specified in the "l=" tag.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: In hash step 2, the Signer/Verifier MUST pass the following to the hash algorithm in the indicated order.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: Each header field MUST be terminated with a single CRLF.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: All tags and their values in the DKIM-Signature header field are included in the cryptographic hash with the sole exception of the value portion of the "b=" (signature) tag, which MUST be treated as the null string.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: All tags MUST be included even if they might not be understood by the Verifier.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: The header field MUST be presented to the hash algorithm after the body of the message rather than with the rest of the header fields and MUST be canonicalized as specified in the "c=" (canonicalization) tag.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: The DKIM-Signature header field MUST NOT be included in its own "h=" tag, although other DKIM- Signature header fields MAY be signed (see Section 4).

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: When calculating the hash on messages that will be transmitted using base64 or quoted-printable encoding, Signers MUST compute the hash after the encoding.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: Likewise, the Verifier MUST incorporate the

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: However, the hash MUST be computed before transport-level encodings such as SMTP "dot-stuffing" (the modification of lines beginning with a "." to avoid confusion with the SMTP end-of-message marker, as specified in [RFC5321]).

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: DKIM messages MAY be either in plain-text or in MIME format; no special treatment is afforded to MIME content.

requirements.heading: Computing the Message Hashes
requirements.text: Message attachments in MIME format MUST be included in the content that is signed.

requirements.heading: Input Requirements
requirements.text: Therefore, Signers and Verifiers SHOULD take reasonable steps to ensure that the messages they are processing are valid according to [RFC5322], [RFC2045], and any other relevant message format standards.

requirements.heading: Output Requirements
requirements.text: For each signature that verifies successfully or produces a TEMPFAIL result, output of the DKIM algorithm MUST include the set of:

requirements.heading: Output Requirements
requirements.text: The output MAY include other signature properties or result meta- data, including PERMFAILed or otherwise ignored signatures, for use by modules that consume those results.

requirements.heading: Signing by Parent Domains
requirements.text: In order to limit the capability of such keys when this is not intended, the "s" flag MAY be set in the "t=" tag of the key record, to constrain the validity of the domain of the AUID.

requirements.heading: Signing by Parent Domains
requirements.text: If the referenced key record contains the "s" flag as part of the "t=" tag, the domain of the AUID ("i=" flag) MUST be the same as that of the SDID (d=) domain.

requirements.heading: Signing by Parent Domains
requirements.text: If this flag is absent, the domain of the AUID MUST be the same as, or a subdomain of, the SDID.

requirements.heading: Relationship between SDID and AUID
requirements.text: DKIM MAY optionally provide a single responsible Agent or User Identifier (AUID).

requirements.heading: Relationship between SDID and AUID
requirements.text: Upon successfully verifying the signature, a receive-side DKIM Verifier MUST communicate the Signing Domain Identifier (d=) to a consuming Identity Assessor module and MAY communicate the Agent or User Identifier (i=) if present.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: A Signer MAY sign previously existing DKIM-Signature header fields using the method described in Section 5.4 to sign trace header fields.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: A Signer MAY add more than one DKIM-Signature header field using different parameters.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: Signers SHOULD NOT remove any DKIM-Signature header fields from messages they are signing, even if they know that the signatures cannot be verified.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: When evaluating a message with multiple signatures, a Verifier SHOULD evaluate signatures independently and on their own merits.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: Verifiers MAY process signatures in any order of their choice; for example, some Verifiers might choose to process signatures corresponding to the From field in the message header before other signatures.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: Verifiers SHOULD continue to check signatures until a signature successfully verifies to the satisfaction of the Verifier.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: To limit potential denial-of-service attacks, Verifiers MAY limit the total number of signatures they will attempt to verify.

requirements.heading: Interpretation
requirements.text: If a Verifier module reports signatures whose evaluations produced PERMFAIL results, Identity Assessors SHOULD ignore those signatures (see Section 6.1), acting as though they were not present in the message.

requirements.heading: Normalize the Message to Prevent Transport Conversions
requirements.text: In order to minimize the chances of such breakage, Signers SHOULD convert the message to a suitable MIME content-transfer encoding such as quoted-printable or base64 as described in [RFC2045] before signing.

requirements.heading: Normalize the Message to Prevent Transport Conversions
requirements.text: Such conversion is outside the scope of DKIM; the actual message SHOULD be converted to 7-bit MIME by an MUA or MSA prior to presentation to the DKIM algorithm.

requirements.heading: Normalize the Message to Prevent Transport Conversions
requirements.text: If the message is submitted to the Signer with any local encoding that will be modified before transmission, that modification to canonical [RFC5322] form MUST be done before signing.

requirements.heading: Normalize the Message to Prevent Transport Conversions
requirements.text: separator convention) MUST be converted to the SMTP-standard CRLF sequence before the message is signed.

requirements.heading: Normalize the Message to Prevent Transport Conversions
requirements.text: Any conversion of this sort SHOULD be applied to the message actually sent to the recipient(s), not just to the version presented to the signing algorithm.

requirements.heading: Normalize the Message to Prevent Transport Conversions
requirements.text: More generally, the Signer MUST sign the message as it is expected to be received by the Verifier rather than in some local or internal form.

requirements.heading: Body Length Limits
requirements.text: A body length count MAY be specified to limit the signature calculation to an initial prefix of the body text, measured in octets.

requirements.heading: Body Length Limits
requirements.text: The body length count MUST be calculated following the canonicalization algorithm; for example, any whitespace ignored by a canonicalization algorithm is not included as part of the body length count.

requirements.heading: Determine the Header Fields to Sign
requirements.text: The From header field MUST be signed (that is, included in the "h=" tag of the resulting DKIM-Signature header field).

requirements.heading: Determine the Header Fields to Sign
requirements.text: Signers SHOULD NOT sign an existing header field likely to be legitimately modified or removed in transit.

requirements.heading: Determine the Header Fields to Sign
requirements.text: Signers MAY include any other header fields present at the time of signing at the discretion of the Signer.

requirements.heading: Determine the Header Fields to Sign
requirements.text: The DKIM-Signature header field is always implicitly signed and MUST NOT be included in the "h=" tag except to indicate that other preexisting signatures are also signed.

requirements.heading: Determine the Header Fields to Sign
requirements.text: Signers MAY claim to have signed header fields that do not exist (that is, Signers MAY include the header field name in the "h=" tag even if that header field does not exist in the message).

requirements.heading: Determine the Header Fields to Sign
requirements.text: When computing the signature, the nonexisting header field MUST be treated as the null string (including the header field name, header field value, all punctuation, and the trailing CRLF).

requirements.heading: Recommended Signature Content
requirements.text: o From (REQUIRED; see Section 5.4)

requirements.heading: Recommended Signature Content
requirements.text: Signers SHOULD choose canonicalization algorithms based on the types of messages they process and their aversion to risk.

requirements.heading: Signatures Involving Multiple Instances of a Field
requirements.text: Signers choosing to sign an existing header field that occurs more than once in the message (such as Received) MUST sign the physically last instance of that header field in the header block.

requirements.heading: Signatures Involving Multiple Instances of a Field
requirements.text: Signers wishing to sign multiple instances of such a header field MUST include the header field name multiple times in the "h=" tag of the DKIM-Signature header field and MUST sign such header fields in order from the bottom of the header field block to the top.

requirements.heading: Signatures Involving Multiple Instances of a Field
requirements.text: The Signer MAY include more instances of a header field name in "h=" than there are actual corresponding header fields so that the signature will not verify if additional header fields of that name are added.

requirements.heading: Compute the Message Hash and Signature
requirements.text: The Signer MUST compute the message hash as described in Section 3.7 and then sign it using the selected public-key algorithm.

requirements.heading: Compute the Message Hash and Signature
requirements.text: Entities such as mailing list managers that implement DKIM and that modify the message or a header field (for example, inserting unsubscribe information) before retransmitting the message SHOULD check any existing signature on input and MUST make such modifications before re-signing the message.

requirements.heading: Insert the DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Finally, the Signer MUST insert the DKIM-Signature header field created in the previous step prior to transmitting the email.

requirements.heading: Insert the DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The DKIM-Signature header field MUST be the same as used to compute the hash as described above, except that the value of the "b=" tag MUST be the appropriately signed hash computed in the previous step, signed using the algorithm specified in the "a=" tag of the DKIM- Signature header field and using the private key corresponding to the selector given in the "s=" tag of the DKIM-Signature header field, as chosen above in Section 5.2.

requirements.heading: Insert the DKIM-Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The DKIM-Signature header field MUST be inserted before any other DKIM-Signature fields in the header block.

requirements.heading: Verifier Actions
requirements.text: Since a Signer MAY remove or revoke a public key at any time, it is advised that verification occur in a timely manner.

requirements.heading: Verifier Actions
requirements.text: A border or intermediate MTA MAY verify the message signature(s).

requirements.heading: Verifier Actions
requirements.text: An MTA who has performed verification MAY communicate the result of that verification by adding a verification header field to incoming messages.

requirements.heading: Verifier Actions
requirements.text: A verifying MTA MAY implement a policy with respect to unverifiable mail, regardless of whether or not it applies the verification header field to signed messages.

requirements.heading: Verifier Actions
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST produce a result that is semantically equivalent to applying the steps listed in Sections 6.1, 6.1.1, and 6.1.2 in order.

requirements.heading: Extract Signatures from the Message
requirements.text: The order in which Verifiers try DKIM-Signature header fields is not defined; Verifiers MAY try signatures in any order they like.

requirements.heading: Extract Signatures from the Message
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST NOT attribute ultimate meaning to the order of multiple DKIM-Signature header fields.

requirements.heading: Extract Signatures from the Message
requirements.text: Therefore, a Verifier SHOULD NOT treat a message that has one or more bad signatures and no good signatures differently from a message with no signature at all.

requirements.heading: Extract Signatures from the Message
requirements.text: A Verifier MAY limit the number of signatures it tries, in order to avoid denial-of-service attacks (see Section 8.4 for further discussion).

requirements.heading: Extract Signatures from the Message
requirements.text: In the following description, text reading "return status (explanation)" (where "status" is one of "PERMFAIL" or "TEMPFAIL") means that the Verifier MUST immediately cease processing that signature.

requirements.heading: Extract Signatures from the Message
requirements.text: The Verifier SHOULD proceed to the next signature, if one

requirements.heading: Extract Signatures from the Message
requirements.text: A Verifier MAY either arrange to defer the message for later processing or try another signature; if no good signature is found and any of the signatures resulted in a TEMPFAIL status, the Verifier MAY arrange to defer the message for later processing.

requirements.heading: Extract Signatures from the Message
requirements.text: Verifiers that are prepared to validate multiple signature header fields SHOULD proceed to the next signature header field, if one exists.

requirements.heading: Extract Signatures from the Message
requirements.text: However, Verifiers MAY make note of the fact that an invalid signature was present for consideration at a later step.

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Implementers MUST meticulously validate the format and values in the DKIM-Signature header field; any inconsistency or unexpected values MUST cause the header field to be completely ignored and the Verifier to return PERMFAIL (signature syntax error).

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST return PERMFAIL (incompatible version) when presented a DKIM-Signature header field with a "v=" tag that is inconsistent with this specification.

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: If any tag listed as "required" in Section 3.5 is omitted from the DKIM-Signature header field, the Verifier MUST ignore the DKIM- Signature header field and return PERMFAIL (signature missing required tag).

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: If the DKIM-Signature header field does not contain the "i=" tag, the Verifier MUST behave as though the value of that tag were "@d", where "d" is the value from the "d=" tag.

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST confirm that the domain specified in the "d=" tag is the same as or a parent domain of the domain part of the "i=" tag.

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: If not, the DKIM-Signature header field MUST be ignored, and the Verifier should return PERMFAIL (domain mismatch).

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: If the "h=" tag does not include the From header field, the Verifier MUST ignore the DKIM-Signature header field and return PERMFAIL (From field not signed).

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Verifiers MAY ignore the DKIM-Signature header field and return PERMFAIL (signature expired) if it contains an "x=" tag and the signature has expired.

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Verifiers MAY ignore the DKIM-Signature header field if the domain used by the Signer in the "d=" tag is not associated with a valid signing entity.

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: The list of unacceptable domains SHOULD be configurable.

requirements.heading: Validate the Signature Header Field
requirements.text: Verifiers MAY ignore the DKIM-Signature header field and return PERMFAIL (unacceptable signature header) for any other reason, for example, if the signature does not sign header fields that the Verifier views to be essential.

requirements.heading: Get the Public Key
requirements.text: The Verifier MUST validate the key record and MUST ignore any public-key records that are malformed.

requirements.heading: Get the Public Key
requirements.text: When validating a message, a Verifier MUST perform the following steps in a manner that is semantically the same as performing them in the order indicated; in some cases, the implementation may parallelize or reorder these steps, as long as the semantics remain unchanged:

requirements.heading: Get the Public Key
requirements.text: If the query for the public key fails to respond, the Verifier MAY seek a later verification attempt by returning TEMPFAIL (key unavailable).

requirements.heading: Get the Public Key
requirements.text: If the query for the public key fails because the corresponding key record does not exist, the Verifier MUST immediately return PERMFAIL (no key for signature).

requirements.heading: Get the Public Key
requirements.text: If the result returned from the query does not adhere to the format defined in this specification, the Verifier MUST ignore the key record and return PERMFAIL (key syntax error).

requirements.heading: Get the Public Key
requirements.text: In particular, the Verifier MUST ignore keys with a version code ("v=" tag) that they do not implement.

requirements.heading: Get the Public Key
requirements.text: If the "h=" tag exists in the public-key record and the hash algorithm implied by the "a=" tag in the DKIM-Signature header field is not included in the contents of the "h=" tag, the Verifier MUST ignore the key record and return PERMFAIL (inappropriate hash algorithm).

requirements.heading: Get the Public Key
requirements.text: If the public-key data (the "p=" tag) is empty, then this key has been revoked and the Verifier MUST treat this as a failed signature check and return PERMFAIL (key revoked).

requirements.heading: Get the Public Key
requirements.text: If the public-key data is not suitable for use with the algorithm and key types defined by the "a=" and "k=" tags in the DKIM- Signature header field, the Verifier MUST immediately return PERMFAIL (inappropriate key algorithm).

requirements.heading: Compute the Verification
requirements.text: When matching header field names in the "h=" tag against the actual message header field, comparisons MUST be case-insensitive.

requirements.heading: Compute the Verification
requirements.text: If the hash does not match, the Verifier SHOULD ignore the signature and return PERMFAIL (body hash did not verify).

requirements.heading: Compute the Verification
requirements.text: If the signature does not validate, the Verifier SHOULD ignore the signature and return PERMFAIL (signature did not verify).

requirements.heading: Communicate Verification Results
requirements.text: Any such header field SHOULD be inserted before any existing DKIM-Signature or preexisting authentication status header fields in the header field block.

requirements.heading: Communicate Verification Results
requirements.text: The Authentication-Results: header field ([RFC5451]) MAY be used for this purpose.

requirements.heading: Communicate Verification Results
requirements.text: To circumvent this attack, Verifiers MAY wish to request deletion of existing results header fields after verification and before arranging to add a new header field.

requirements.heading: Interpret Results/Apply Local Policy
requirements.text: In general, modules that consume DKIM verification output SHOULD NOT determine message acceptability based solely on a lack of any signature or on an unverifiable signature; such rejection would cause severe interoperability problems.

requirements.heading: Interpret Results/Apply Local Policy
requirements.text: If an MTA does wish to reject such messages during an SMTP session (for example, when communicating with a peer who, by prior agreement, agrees to only send signed messages), and a signature is missing or does not verify, the handling MTA SHOULD use a 550/5.7.x reply code.

requirements.heading: Interpret Results/Apply Local Policy
requirements.text: Where the Verifier is integrated within the MTA and it is not possible to fetch the public key, perhaps because the key server is not available, a temporary failure message MAY be generated using a 451/4.7.5 reply code, such as:

requirements.heading: Interpret Results/Apply Local Policy
requirements.text: Temporary failures such as inability to access the key server or other external service are the only conditions that SHOULD use a 4xx SMTP reply code.

requirements.heading: Interpret Results/Apply Local Policy
requirements.text: In particular, cryptographic signature verification failures MUST NOT provoke 4xx SMTP replies.

requirements.heading: Interpret Results/Apply Local Policy
requirements.text: Once the signature has been verified, that information MUST be conveyed to the Identity Assessor (such as an explicit allow/ whitelist and reputation system) and/or to the end user.

requirements.heading: Interpret Results/Apply Local Policy
requirements.text: If the SDID is not the same as the address in the From: header field, the mail system SHOULD take pains to ensure that the actual SDID is clear to the reader.

requirements.heading: Interpret Results/Apply Local Policy
requirements.text: For diagnostic purposes, the exact reason why the verification fails SHOULD be made available and possibly recorded in the system logs.

requirements.heading: Interpret Results/Apply Local Policy
requirements.text: If the email cannot be verified, then it SHOULD be treated the same as all unverified email, regardless of whether or not it looks like it was signed.

requirements.heading: IANA Considerations
requirements.text: All registrations into these namespaces MUST include the name being registered, the document in which it was registered or updated, and an indication of its current status, which MUST be one of "active" (in current use) or "historic" (no longer in current use).

requirements.heading: Intentionally Malformed Key Records
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST thoroughly verify all key records retrieved from the DNS and be robust against intentionally as well as unintentionally malformed key records.

requirements.heading: Intentionally Malformed DKIM-Signature Header Fields
requirements.text: Verifiers MUST be prepared to receive messages with malformed DKIM- Signature header fields and thoroughly verify the header field before depending on any of its contents.

requirements.heading: Inappropriate Signing by Parent Domains
requirements.text: Note that a Verifier MAY ignore signatures that come from an unlikely domain such as ".com", as discussed in Section 6.1.1.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: Although the "g=" tag has been deprecated in this version of the DKIM specification (and thus MUST now be ignored), Signers are advised not to include the "g=" tag in key records because some [RFC4871]- compliant Verifiers will be in use for a considerable period to come.
